extracted.intended_audience: people learning Russian (beginners seeking online resources)
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory resource overview for beginners learning Russian online, outlining practical steps (phrases, vocabulary, practice) and reasons to study the language. The page points to phrase lists, themed vocabulary, and options to find language partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick up some basic phrases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site offers 'Phrases' — Russian phrases sorted into useful everyday topics to help learners acquire practical, everyday language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand your vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the site's 'Vocabulary' section — vocabulary divided into themed lists to build topic-specific word knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a language partner to practise with
rubrics_metrics.description: find a language partner to practise with
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recommends practising with a language partner as part of learning; no specific pairing guidance is provided on this page beyond suggesting it as a resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn the Cyrillic alphabet
rubrics_metrics.description: It is written with the Cyrillic alphabet which consists of 33 letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that Russian uses the 33-letter Cyrillic alphabet, implying that learning the script is a foundational step for reading and writing Russian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn motivations and use-cases for studying Russian
rubrics_metrics.description: So why learn Russian? Business, Literature, Travel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists benefits/motivations — business opportunities, a rich literary tradition (Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Pushkin, Chekhov), and travel utility — as reasons that can inform learner goals and focus areas.
